data.name: ResizeHandleTooltip
data.value: Drag to resize · arrow keys nudge by 1 MiB (hold Shift for 1 GiB)

data.name: NotAdminBadge
data.value: Not running as administrator — cloning is disabled

data.name: FreeSpaceLeaveDesc
data.value: Leaves the extra space unallocated — use it later in Disk Management

data.name: FreeSpaceMergeTitle
data.value: Add it to the last partition

data.name: FreeSpaceMergeDesc
data.value: Simple and safe · works on MBR disks too. If the last partition is a recovery one, that grows instead

data.name: FreeSpaceResizeDesc
data.value: Grow a middle partition like C: · GPT and MBR sources (not extended partitions)

data.name: ResizeHelp
data.value: “New total size” is the final size after growing — not how much to add. If it isn’t grown automatically during the clone, finish up with the “Expand partition” button on the results screen. Only NTFS partitions can be grown.

data.name: VssDesc
data.value: Captures a consistent copy even if files change mid-clone

data.name: VerifyDesc
data.value: Reads the copy back and compares it to the source · roughly doubles the time

data.name: SkipBadDesc
data.value: Fills unreadable sectors with zeros and keeps going

data.name: SmartDesc
data.value: Copies only the used blocks, so it’s faster · needs a snapshot

data.name: NewHwDesc
data.value: Enables storage drivers so it still boots on a different PC

data.name: AutoUefiDesc
data.value: When the source is BIOS/MBR, converts the clone to GPT/UEFI after cloning so it boots on NVMe / UEFI-only PCs. Irreversible (changes the target only; source untouched). No effect on GPT sources.

data.name: BootUsbHint
data.value: Creates a rescue USB for a PC that won't start Windows at all. Boot from this USB and DiskMigrator-X launches right away for backup, restore, and boot repair. Built from this PC's built-in recovery environment — no downloads (takes a few minutes).

data.name: BootUsbWarn
data.value: Everything on this USB will be erased. At least 2 GB and a USB (removable) disk are required.

data.name: BootUsbNoTarget
data.value: Choose the USB disk to turn into a boot USB.

data.name: BootUsbNotUsb
data.value: For safety, only USB (removable) disks can be used.

data.name: BootUsbTooSmall
data.value: The USB is too small — at least 2 GB is required.

data.name: BootUsbAfterHint
data.value: How to use: plug the USB into the PC to rescue, power it on, and pick the USB (UEFI) entry in the boot menu (usually F12/F11/F8). DiskMigrator-X starts automatically.

data.name: PeNoIngredients
data.value: Could not find the boot-USB ingredients (recovery environment) on this PC.

data.name: PeCancelled
data.value: Cancelled. The USB may be incomplete — please create it again.

data.name: FixBootHint
data.value: Use this when a cloned or restored disk won't boot. Connect that disk to this PC (e.g. via USB) and inspect it — no copying involved, only the boot configuration is checked and repaired.

data.name: FixBootReadOnlyNote
data.value: The check is read-only and safe. If a problem is found, a repair button appears.

data.name: FixBootBlockedSystem
data.value: Boot repair is not applied to the currently running system disk — this PC already booted from it, so there is nothing to fix.

data.name: BackupIncNoticeFmt
data.value: Existing backup found — this will be an incremental backup: only what changed since {0} is saved to the new file {1}. Existing files are never modified. When restoring, pick the most recent file, and keep the files together in the same folder.

data.name: BackupChainBroken
data.value: The base backup (first file of the chain) could not be found, so an incremental backup is not possible. Do a full backup under a new file name.

data.name: BackupHint
data.value: Saves the selected disk as a single .vhdx image — smart clone stores only used areas, VSS keeps it consistent. Restore it later with 'Restore image'.

data.name: BackupRecommendTitle
data.value: Save your current PC (C:\) whole into a single file (recommended)

data.name: BackupRecommendDesc
data.value: Even if you replace the disk or it fails, one restore brings your PC back exactly as it was.

data.name: BackupCancelledMsg
data.value: Backup cancelled. The image file being created may be incomplete.

data.name: ImageQuickOkFmt
data.value: Image OK: {0} partition(s) recognized — structure intact. A deep check (chkdsk) runs again when restore starts.

data.name: ImageQuickBad
data.value: The image could not be read — the file may be corrupted or not a valid VHDX.

data.name: RestoreHint
data.value: Writes the selected .vhdx image onto the target disk in full. If the target is larger than the image, the extra space is made usable; if it is smaller, the image is shrunk automatically to fit. 'Prepare for new hardware' makes it boot on a different PC.

data.name: ShrinkTempNoneFmt
data.value: A shrink clone internally backs up the source to a temporary image, shrinks it, and restores it. No disk (other than the source and target) has enough free space ({0} or more) for the temporary image. Free up space on another disk and try again.

data.name: ShrinkAutoFmt
data.value: The target is smaller than the image — partition {0} will be shrunk automatically from {1} to {2} for the restore. Later partitions are pulled forward, and the original image is preserved. (If the actual data is larger than that, the restore stops with a clear error.)

data.name: ShrinkAutoNoCandidate
data.value: The target is smaller than the image, and the image has no NTFS partition that can be shrunk. Choose a larger target.

data.name: ShrinkAutoTooSmallFmt
data.value: The target ({0}) is too small — the image will not fit even after shrinking. Choose a larger target.

data.name: RestoreWarn
data.value: This overwrites all data on the target disk and cannot be undone. Double-check the target disk.

data.name: RestoreCancelledMsg
data.value: Restore cancelled. The target disk is incomplete — do not use it.

data.name: IrreversibleWarn
data.value: This can’t be undone. Double-check the target disk.

data.name: DoNotDisconnect
data.value: Don’t disconnect the target disk or shut down the PC while this is running.

data.name: BootCheckTip
data.value: Inspects the bootloader, BCD, winload and storage drivers — without actually booting.

data.name: ForceRepairTip
data.value: The check found no problems. If this disk still won't boot, you can run the repair anyway — it rewrites the boot configuration, prepares the storage drivers so the disk boots on other hardware, and commits the changes to the disk.

data.name: RepairBootTip
data.value: Repoints the BCD device references to this disk’s partitions to fix error 0xc000000e.

data.name: MakeBootableTitle
data.value: Make it boot on modern PCs (convert to GPT/UEFI)

data.name: MakeBootableDesc
data.value: This copy uses the same legacy BIOS layout as the source, so it only boots on PCs that still support legacy boot. It won’t boot from an NVMe M.2 slot or on UEFI-only PCs. The button below converts it to GPT and creates an EFI system partition so it boots under UEFI.

data.name: ConvertUefiTip
data.value: Can’t be undone. Afterwards, turn off CSM in the BIOS and boot the UEFI entry.

data.name: Converting
data.value: Converting… (this can take a few minutes)

data.name: SafeRemoveDesc
data.value: Once the clone finishes, the target disk is brought back online and Windows auto-mounts the copied volumes. In that state, Windows blocks "Safely Remove Hardware" with a "device is in use" error. The button below dismounts the volumes and takes the disk offline so you can just unplug the USB.

data.name: SafeRemoveTip
data.value: Takes the disk offline (same as "Offline" in Disk Management) and flushes its caches. Once you see the confirmation, unplug the USB. Your cloned data is not affected.

data.name: SafeRemoveDone
data.value: The target disk is now offline. You can safely unplug the USB.

data.name: SafeRemoveFailFmt
data.value: Safe removal failed: {0} — In Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc), right-click this disk, choose "Offline," then unplug it.

data.name: ExpandPartitionTip
data.value: Grows the resized partition — or the last one — into the leftover unallocated space. If a recovery partition is last, that grows instead. Works most reliably with the target connected on its own, with the source disconnected.

data.name: EulaDanger
data.value: This program can permanently erase everything on the target (write) disk. Please read the terms below and agree before continuing.

data.name: EulaAgreeCheck
data.value: I have read and understood the above, and I agree.

data.name: ConfirmPromptFmt
data.value: To continue, type the target disk’s model name exactly — {0}

data.name: BlockChooseSourceTarget
data.value: Choose a source disk and a target disk.

data.name: BlockConfirmIncomplete
data.value: Can’t start yet — the confirmation isn’t complete.

data.name: TargetNotFoundAgain
data.value: Couldn’t find the target disk again.

data.name: ActionAfter
data.value: How it will look after cloning

data.name: TrailingFreeFmt
data.value: Trailing free space {0} — this much isn’t cloned when moving to a smaller disk.

data.name: UnallocatedTipLine2
data.value: Belongs to no partition, so it isn’t cloned.

data.name: FreeSpaceHeaderFmt
data.value: What to do with {0} of free space

data.name: ProgSnapshotting
data.value: Creating snapshot… (up to tens of seconds)

data.name: VerdictReady
data.value: Ready to boot — all critical checks passed

data.name: VerdictReadyWarn
data.value: Bootable, but with warnings — review the warning items below

data.name: VerdictNoBoot
data.value: Boot at risk — a critical check failed

data.name: VerdictUnknown
data.value: Can’t tell — a critical item couldn’t be checked (make sure the target is online and mounted)

data.name: FailNothingWritten
data.value: Nothing was written to the target disk.

data.name: ResSnapshotTimeFmt
data.value: Snapshot taken: {0} (changes after this point weren’t cloned)

data.name: ResVerifyPass
data.value: Verification: passed — source and target match.

data.name: ResVerifyFail
data.value: Verification: failed — source and target don’t match.

data.name: ResBadSectorsFmt
data.value: Bad sectors: {0} filled with zeros. Files at those locations may be damaged.

data.name: ResMsgCompletedFmt
data.value: [{0}] {1} is now an exact copy of the source.

data.name: ResTitleBadSectors
data.value: Clone complete, but there were bad sectors

data.name: ResMsgBadSectorsFmt
data.value: {0} sectors that couldn’t be read from the source were filled with zeros. Most files are fine, but some may be damaged — check your important data.

data.name: ResMsgCancelledFmt
data.value: [{0}] {1} is incomplete. Don’t boot from this disk or use its data.

data.name: ResTitleResizeCorrupted
data.value: Cloned, but the partition layout is broken — don’t boot from this disk

data.name: ResMsgResizeCorruptedFmt
data.value: Data was copied to [{0}] {1}, but rewriting the GPT to reflect the resized layout failed, so the partition table points to the old positions. Don’t boot from this disk or use its data. Turn off resize and clone again.

data.name: RbNotGptFmt
data.value: The source is {0} format, so this can’t be used — this method moves partitions and rewrites the partition table.

data.name: RbExtended
data.value: The source has an extended partition (logical drives), so this can’t be used — logical drives are linked by an EBR chain, and moving them means rewriting the whole chain.

data.name: RbMbr2tb
data.value: An MBR source can only address partition locations up to about 2 TB, so this can’t be used on a larger target. Use “Add it to the last partition”, or convert the source to GPT.

data.name: RbSectorMismatchFmt
data.value: The source and target have different sector sizes (source {0} bytes, target {1} bytes). Partition positions won’t line up, so this can’t be used.

data.name: RbNoNtfs
data.value: The source has no NTFS partition that can be grown.

data.name: RbNoRoom
data.value: The target isn’t larger than the source, so there’s no room to grow.

data.name: ReagentcNote
data.value: The recovery partition moved back, so it’s no longer where Windows remembered it. After booting the cloned disk, run reagentc /enable once in an administrator command prompt to reconnect the recovery environment. (Windows itself boots fine.)

data.name: FailSeeLog
data.value: Check the log file for details.

data.name: CloseRunningMsg2
data.value: If you close now, the target disk will be left incomplete and its data will be unusable.

data.name: CloseRunningMsg3
data.value: Are you sure you want to close?

data.name: McpIntro
data.value: Opens a channel that works only inside this computer. Claude can read disk state, boot configuration and backup images directly, and point out what is wrong. It only reads — changing a disk is still something you do here, yourself.

data.name: McpRunningHint
data.value: The connection is open. Put the address and token below into Claude's MCP settings. Closing the app closes the connection too.

data.name: McpShareDetails
data.value: Also send disk serials and volume names

data.name: McpShareDetailsHint
data.value: Masked by default. Diagnostics end up in the conversation log, so turn this on only when needed.

data.name: McpStoppedHint
data.value: Connection closed. Opening it again issues a new token.

data.name: McpTitle
data.value: Let Claude read this app's diagnostics

data.name: ProposalConfirmNote
data.value: Applying does not start anything. You must type the target model name before it can run.

data.name: ProposalDiskGone
data.value: The proposed disks were not found — the connection seems to have changed. Refresh and try again.

data.name: ProposalPlainNote
data.value: Applying fills in the selection. You still press Start yourself.

data.name: DiagNotOnTarget
data.value: That location is on the disk being diagnosed. Choose a USB drive or another disk — a report must never be written to the disk it describes.

data.name: DiagIncludeHint
data.value: Masked by default. This file is meant to be shown to someone else.

data.name: DiagSavedFmt
data.value: Saved to {0} ({1:N0} KB). On a working PC, show this file to Claude — or send it to us.

data.name: DiagSaveHint
data.value: Gathers this disk's boot information into a single file. The disk is not modified. Take the file to another PC to get help.

data.name: DiagCollecting
data.value: Collecting… reading only, nothing is written to the disk.

data.name: DiagIncludeDetails
data.value: Include disk serials and volume names

data.name: McpRunningReusedHint
data.value: The connection is open with the same address and token as last time — if you have already put them into Claude, nothing needs changing.

data.name: McpResetTokenHint
data.value: Use this if you think the token leaked. The old one stops working and you must paste the new one into Claude.

data.name: McpTokenReset
data.value: A new token was issued. Copy it into Claude again.

data.name: McpActivityHint
data.value: Every call goes through here. Read means the disk was only read; Suggestion means a card was put on screen - nothing ran.

data.name: McpActivityEmpty
data.value: Nothing yet. Calls will appear here as Claude works.

data.name: VerdictDiskOffline
data.value: This disk is OFFLINE, so its volumes are not mounted and nothing could be checked. Bring it online first (Disk Management, or diskpart: select disk N -> online disk), then check again.

data.name: McpConnectorCopied
data.value: Copied the address with the token. Paste it into the address field of the Add connector screen.

data.name: McpConnectorHint
data.value: For tools that cannot send a header and must carry the token in the address. It does not work in Claude's settings screen. This line contains your key — do not show it to anyone.

data.name: McpCommandLabel
data.value: Command to connect Claude (this is the way that works)

data.name: McpCommandCopied
data.value: Copied the connect command. Paste and run it in a command window.

data.name: McpCommandHint
data.value: Copy it with the button below, then paste and run it in a command window. Adding it as a connector in Claude's settings screen does not work — that screen only accepts https addresses, and this channel is plain http because it works inside this computer only.

data.name: McpConnectHint
data.value: This button registers the app with Claude for you. No command window, no copying addresses or tokens. You will see exactly what will be changed first, and the original settings are kept as a copy.

data.name: McpConnectNoBridge
data.value: The file this needs (DiskMigratorX.Bridge.exe) is not next to the app. Reinstalling from the installer includes it. Until then, use the manual command below.

data.name: McpConnectDesktopDone
data.value: Registered. Quit Claude completely and start it again.

data.name: McpConnectCodeDone
data.value: Registered. Restart any window that is already open.

data.name: McpConnectConfirmBodyFmt
McpAdvancedLabel
data.value: Connect manually (if the button does not work)

data.name: AskHint
data.value: No switching windows. Press this and Claude reads your disks with this app's tools and writes what is wrong right here. If you have picked a disk, it looks at that one. This can take a few minutes.

data.name: ChatInputHint
data.value: Feel free to keep asking — "why is that?", "can I clone it now?". It remembers what you talked about. If you swapped a disk, start over with [New chat].

data.name: AskNeedsClaudeCode
data.value: Asking from here needs Claude Code on this computer. That is fine if you do not have it — use [Connect to Claude] below and ask from the Claude window instead.

data.name: AskDisclaimer
data.value: Claude only reads. Cloning, backup, restore and boot repair are still yours to do on this screen.

data.name: DiagSaveExpander
data.value: Save a diagnostic file (to analyse on another computer)

data.name: ClaudeNotInstalled
data.value: No Claude Code — only the asking feature is unavailable

data.name: ClaudeLoginFailedFmt
data.value: Could not open the sign-in window. Run {0} in a command window instead.
